presets.caveat: ODIS measures conditions around a school, not the school or its students.
presets.label: Where stress concentrates
presets.narration: All 23,595 US public high schools, colored by the neighborhood around each. The bright band is the South: median Composite Score 33 against 28 nationally, and more stressed than a school elsewhere in 77% of pairings. Yet 45% of the differences lie between counties of the same state, against 28% between regions, so zoom in.

presets.caveat: An association across neighborhoods, not proof that wiring homes would raise degrees.
presets.label: Digital divide, education divide
presets.narration: Where more households lack broadband, fewer adults hold a college degree: ρ = 0.69 across 23,404 schools, the second-strongest link across domains. Even with 10 other conditions held fixed, missing broadband is the strongest predictor of low adult attainment, 5.5 points per standard deviation (SD).

presets.caveat: Regions are a choice, and states within one region can differ as much as regions do.
presets.label: Same pair, different regions
presets.narration: Education and health stress rise together, but how tightly depends on the region: ρ = 0.65 in California and 0.59 in the Northeast, only 0.29 in the South (p < 0.001). 8 of the 10 domain pairs differ by region; the panel recomputes this one live for California and Florida.

presets.caveat: ODIS housing is vacancy, affordability, and park access; it does not measure homelessness.
presets.label: Housing runs backwards in the West
presets.narration: Nationally, Housing barely moves with the other domains (ρ = 0.05 to 0.27). In California and the Pacific Northwest it runs backwards: unaffordable housing sits in otherwise less stressed places (ρ = −0.51), which a composite ranking would miss. In the South, housing is barely tied to the rest (ρ = 0.08).

presets.caveat: Graduation is one outcome, and these are associations within states, not causes.
presets.label: One formula does not fit everywhere
presets.narration: The composite weighs domains equally everywhere; graduation does not. One SD more Health stress goes with 4.7 points lower graduation in the Midwest but 1.3 in the Northeast, and Crime, 45% of the composite's spread, predicts it in no region. Reweighting moves 52% of schools 10+ percentiles. Oneida County's lake schools, selected here, top the vacancy scale from vacation homes and fall from the 92nd to the 14th.

presets.caveat: This is where the numbers point, not proof of what policy would work.
presets.label: Where a lawmaker would look first
presets.narration: If graduation is the goal, start with Health, the domain that tracks it: 3.4 to 7.4 points per SD in the Midwest, South, and Mountain & Southwest. Within regions, the numbers point to infant mortality and violent crime in the Midwest (ρ = 0.68, 0.60) and to single-parent households and missing broadband in the South (0.55, 0.49).
